newsitem.title: USA: "Evita" takes top honors at Golden Globes awards.
newsitem.headline: "Evita" takes top honors at Golden Globes awards.

text.p: "Evita", the epic musical starring pop star Madonna, led the list of winners at Sunday night's Golden Globe Awards.
The film won three of the awards presented by the Hollywood Foreign Press Association, including best actress in a musical or comedy film for Madonna.
It also won the award for best musical or comedy motion picture as well as best original song in a film, "You Must Love Me," from the British duo, composer Andrew Lloyd Webber and lyricist Tim Rice.

"I have been so incredibly blessed this last year. I have so much to be thankful for," Madonna told the star-studded audience at the Beverly Hilton Hotel, referring to the birth of her baby and her role as Argentina's Eva Peron.
Backstage, the blonde singer and dancer said "Evita" was "a great opportunity to challenge myself in my music, singing and dancing. I hope to keep going as an artist and keep making movies."
"The English Patient", which led the Golden Globe field with nominations in seven categories, ended up winning only two awards -- best dramatic picture and best original film score.

Its stars, Ralph Fiennes and Kristin Scott Thomas, were passed over by Golden Globe voters in the best dramatic actor and actress categories, as was Juliette Binoche, nominated for best supporting actress for her role in the wartime drama.

The best motion picture director award went to Milos Forman for "The People vs. Larry Flynt", the life story of the controversial publisher of "Hustler" magazine, starring Woody Harrelson in the title role. Scott Alexander and Larry Karaszewski took the Golden Globe for best motion picture screenplay for their work on the film.

The Golden Globes are seen as a barometer of potential Oscar winners when the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences presents Hollywood's highest honours in March. But unlike the Oscars, the Globes for the most part distinguish between musical/comedy films and dramatic movies and includes TV awards.

Veteran actress Lauren Bacall won a Globe for best supporting actress in a movie for her role in "The Mirror Has Two Faces", while the best supporting actor honour went to Edward Norton for "Primal Fear". Tom Cruise picked up the Globe for best actor in a musical or comedy film for his role in "Jerry Maguire".
In the dramatic film category, Brenda Blethyn won best actress Globe for "Secrets & Lies" and best actor honours went to Geoffrey Rush in "Shine".
"Kolya", produced in the Czech Republic, was voted the best foreign language film.

In the television category, "The X-Files", from the Fox network and HBO's "Rasputin" shared the honours. "The X-Files" took best dramatic TV series, best actress in a dramatic TV series award for Gillian Anderson and best actor in a dramatic TV series Globe for David Duchovny.
"Rasputin" earned Golden Globes for best mini-series or film made for television, best supporting actor in that category for Ian McKellen and best actor for Alan Rickman.
Also in the mini-series or film made for television category, Britain's Helen Mirren took the best actress award for "Losing Chase" and Kathy Bates took best supporting actress for "The Late Shift".

NBC's "3rd Rock From The Sun" won two Golden Globes, for best musical or comedy TV series and best actor in that category for John Lithgow. Helen Hunt garnered a Globe for best actress in a musical or comedy TV series her role in "Mad About You."

The 54th annual Golden Globe Awards also honoured Dustin Hoffman with the Cecil B. DeMille Award for his achievements. "Dustin Hoffman has had a career filled with landmark achievements," Cruise said in a special tribute to Hoffman.
